title: SRAM bit-cell scaling stagnation
bottleneck: SRAM bit cells have stopped shrinking at the pace of logic, so on-chip caches now dominate die area and cost on leading-edge chips. Six-transistor cells are limited by stability margins and leakage, and alternative cells (gain cells, 3D-stacked SRAM) add process complexity. Architects must choose between smaller caches that starve accelerators or larger caches that bloat die size.
why_it_blocks: SRAM area inflation raises the cost of every advanced chip and caps the on-chip memory that mitigates the memory wall. Without denser SRAM, AI accelerators can't keep growing context windows and model sizes without exploding die cost.
current_state: High-density SRAM variants and 3D-stacked cache (e.g., stacked L3 in server CPUs) are shipping, buying incremental density. Fundamental bit-cell scaling remains stalled, with no disruptive replacement in production.
